messages.title: Did Cancellation Stop the Work?
messages.subtitle: The cancel signal arrived, yet a result handoff can stay blocked. Find the operation that must participate.
messages.property: After request R is cancelled, its request-scoped work must not remain indefinitely blocked on an operation with no cancellation path.
messages.takeaway: Checking cancellation before a blocking operation is not the same as making that operation cancellable. The operation that can block must observe the signal.
messages.step.review.title: A pre-check looks reassuring
messages.step.review.lead: A producer checks request cancellation, processes an item, then sends its result. Follow the work path and cancellation path separately.
messages.step.precheck-passes.title: The request is still active
messages.step.precheck-passes.lead: The pre-check reports no cancellation. That is true at this instant; it says nothing about a later blocking send.
messages.step.process-completes.title: Processing finishes
messages.step.process-completes.lead: The producer has a result ready. Completing local computation does not guarantee the result can be handed off.
messages.step.send-starts.title: The result send starts
messages.step.send-starts.lead: The producer enters a blocking handoff. In the Go-shaped example, out <- result waits for a receiver.
messages.step.no-receiver.title: There is no receiver
messages.step.no-receiver.lead: No one is reading from the result channel. The handoff cannot complete yet.
messages.step.send-blocks.title: The producer is blocked
messages.step.send-blocks.lead: The send waits for a receiver. The earlier cancellation check has already finished and will not run again while this send waits.
messages.step.cancel-requested.title: Now the request is cancelled
messages.step.cancel-requested.lead: The cancel signal becomes available after the send blocks. Trace where the signal can reach from here.
messages.step.signal-question.title: What did cancellation establish?
messages.step.signal-question.lead: The request's cancellation signal is observable. Has anything made this blocked send observe it?
messages.step.still-blocked.title: The worker is still blocked
messages.step.still-blocked.lead: Cancellation was signalled successfully. The send still waits only for a receiver, so the request-scoped producer does not terminate.
messages.step.property.title: Name the lifecycle property
messages.step.property.lead: After cancelling request R, its work must not remain indefinitely blocked on an operation without a cancellation path. This does not require instant stop.
messages.step.aware-wait.title: Let the handoff see both outcomes
messages.step.aware-wait.lead: Wait for either a receiver ready to take the result or cancellation becoming active. The blocking boundary itself must participate.
messages.step.replay.title: Replay with a cancellation-aware send
messages.step.replay.lead: The result is ready, no receiver exists, and the producer waits on both handoff readiness and cancellation.
messages.step.cancel-releases.title: Cancellation releases the wait
messages.step.cancel-releases.lead: When cancellation arrives, the producer leaves the handoff without waiting for a receiver. The request-scoped worker can terminate.
messages.step.receiver-ready.title: A receiver can still take the result
messages.step.receiver-ready.lead: Positive control: if a receiver is available, the handoff completes normally. Cancellation awareness must not suppress successful delivery.
messages.step.bounded-local.title: Do tiny local work normally
messages.step.bounded-local.lead: A short bounded calculation does not need to check cancellation after every instruction. Put cooperation where work can block or run too long.
messages.step.cpu-bound.title: Long computation is another boundary
messages.step.cpu-bound.lead: A long CPU task that never checks cancellation may delay termination before it even reaches the handoff. It needs its own cooperative points.
messages.step.downstream.title: A downstream API may ignore cancellation
messages.step.downstream.lead: Passing a request through a non-participating API does not make that call stop. The downstream wait needs a cancellation path too.
messages.step.no-rollback.title: Cancellation is not rollback
messages.step.no-rollback.lead: If a receiver already took the result or an effect committed, cancelling later does not undo it. Lifecycle termination and effect reversal are different claims.
messages.step.remaining.title: Trace every remaining boundary
messages.step.remaining.lead: Other waits, long computation, and downstream calls can still outlive the request. Detached work may intentionally have another owner. Case 08 asks what correctness state survives a process restart.
messages.step.transfer.title: Transfer: shutting down a worker pool
messages.step.transfer.lead: The result queue is full as shutdown begins. Producers have finished computing but block on queue writes. Which operation must observe shutdown so workers can exit?
messages.step.recap.title: Six questions, one lifecycle boundary
messages.step.recap.lead: Follow ownership and blocking points before claiming that cancellation stopped work.
messages.visual.title: Cancellation Propagation
messages.visual.workAware: process ✓ → wait for receiver OR cancel
messages.visual.strongBoundary: send listens for receiver or cancellation
messages.visual.cpuBoundary: long CPU work needs its own checks
messages.rail.evidencePrecheck: The pre-check saw an active request.
messages.rail.evidenceBlocked: The send has no receiver and is blocked.
messages.rail.evidenceCancel: Cancellation is observable; the weak send remains blocked.
messages.rail.evidenceRepair: The repaired handoff waits on both possible outcomes.
messages.rail.evidenceControl: A receiver can still complete the handoff.
messages.rail.contractStrong: The blocking handoff can finish by delivery or cancellation.
messages.rail.contractScope: Other long or downstream operations require their own path.
messages.rail.propertyHidden: What can the blocked send observe?
messages.rail.property: Cancelled request work cannot remain indefinitely at a blocking point with no cancellation path.
messages.challenge.title: What did cancel actually guarantee?
messages.challenge.intro: The producer passed a pre-check, processed its item, and blocked sending to an unreceived channel. Cancellation is now requested.
messages.challenge.question: Which conclusion follows from this trace?
messages.option.signalOnly: The signal is observable, but this send has no path to react to it.
messages.option.forcedStop: Cancel forcibly stopped the blocked send and its producer.
messages.option.rollback: Cancel undid the completed processing and any result already delivered.
messages.challenge.feedback: The signal worked. The weak handoff still waits only for a receiver. A cancellation-aware blocking operation can release the request-scoped worker.
messages.deepDive.title: Where must cancellation intersect the work?
messages.deepDive.section1.title: The minimal stuck producer
messages.deepDive.section1.body: The pre-check passes, processing finishes, and a send blocks without a receiver. Cancellation then becomes observable, but the send never listens for it. The worker remains blocked.
messages.deepDive.section2.title: A participating handoff
messages.deepDive.section2.body: The handoff waits for either a receiver or cancellation. A ready receiver still gets the result; cancellation with no receiver releases the producer. The choice is made at the blocking point.
messages.deepDive.section3.title: What cancellation does not undo
messages.deepDive.section3.body: A completed handoff or committed effect is not rolled back by later cancellation. A short bounded calculation need not check at every instruction; long computation does need cooperative points.
messages.deepDive.section4.title: Other owners and APIs
messages.deepDive.section4.body: A downstream API that ignores cancellation may keep waiting. Intentionally detached work can continue under another explicit lifecycle owner; do not confuse it with request-scoped work.
messages.deepDive.section5.title: The next boundary is restart
messages.deepDive.section5.body: Even a worker that terminates cleanly may restart in a new process. Case 08 asks which correctness state must survive reconstruction.
messages.recap.1: Identity: which request owns this work and result?
messages.recap.2: Authority: who can cancel the request?
messages.recap.3: Durability: which completed effects survive cancellation?
messages.recap.4: Delivery: can the handoff wait indefinitely for a receiver?
messages.recap.5: Ordering: did cancellation happen before or after delivery?
messages.recap.6: Lifecycle: which blocking operation can observe cancel and exit?
